signals.title: JPY/SEK — G10 Bilateral Theme + Geopolitical Shock
signals.text: G10 scorecard prints JPY as top leader at +1.286% (n=7 pairs) against SEK as laggard at -1.634% (n=2 pairs), yielding an extreme bilateral spread of 2.920%. Strait of Hormuz transit disruptions and surging crude oil past $102/bbl drive flight away from European energy importers toward the yen despite JPY's policy rate carrying an accommodative real stance of -1.70%. BoJ policy rate sits at 1.0% against Riksbank at 1.75%, leaving a 75bp nominal deficit that JPY momentum completely overpowers in this risk-sensitive backdrop. The pair reflects systemic energy-shock vulnerability, with SEK weighed down by negative economic surprises at ESI -6.7 while JPY prints strong data momentum at ESI +23.8. Trade bias: Short SEK/JPY; geopolitical energy disruption continues to crush energy-importing beta. Catalyst: US CPI at 12:30 UTC today. Risk: De-escalation headlines in the Middle East compress the bilateral spread back below 1.20%.

signals.title: USD/JPY — Crowded Carry Unwind + Options Skew
signals.text: USD/JPY prints at 154.40, pinned below its SMA20 (157.91), SMA50 (159.85), and SMA200 (158.42) moving-average cluster. CFTC positioning shows JPY leveraged funds net short -111,297 contracts, sitting at the 2nd percentile of its 52-week range with a z-score of -2.18σ, after shedding another 29,678 contracts WoW. The options desk confirms aggressive downside positioning with 1-month 25-delta risk reversals at -2.04, reflecting massive put demand despite 1-month IV sitting at 9.7% versus HV30 of 10.3% (VRP -0.6%). A positive OIS carry buffer of SOFR 3.64% versus TONA 0.98% (+266bp) provides insufficient structural defense as crowded spec shorts unwind amidst rising energy risks. The BEER model tags USD/JPY as severely cheap at z=-2.69σ against fair value 158.52, but technical breakdown and extreme options skew dominate spot action. Trade bias: Short USD/JPY; speculative short-covering forces spot lower through technical resistance. Catalyst: US CPI print at 12:30 UTC today. Risk: Spot closes back above the SMA20 at 157.91, aborting the downside momentum.

signals.title: AUD/USD — Crowded Long + Retail Divergence
signals.text: AUD/USD trades at 0.7158, consolidating just beneath its SMA20 at 0.7164 while holding above the SMA50 at 0.7065. Leveraged funds hold an extended net long of +50,250 contracts, ranking at the 94th percentile of its 52-week distribution (z=+1.79σ), though net additions stalled with a WoW delta of -3,328 contracts. Retail sentiment stands in direct contrarian divergence at 91% short, reflecting heavy retail fading of the prevailing uptrend. The 71bp OIS carry advantage (AONIA 4.35% vs SOFR 3.64%) supports Australian dollar resilience, but options show a mild put skew of -0.55 on IV of 7.0% against HV30 of 6.0%. Late-trend institutional exhaustion meets retail capitulation risk as price tests immediate moving-average resistance. Trade bias: Neutral/long AUD/USD; institutional positioning limits breakout room despite retail short squeeze setup. Catalyst: US CPI release at 12:30 UTC today. Risk: Leveraged funds net positioning drops for a second consecutive week, invalidating the upside momentum thesis.

signals.title: EUR/USD — Macro Tightening + Bear Steepener Pressure
signals.text: EUR/USD trades at 1.1612, hovering below its SMA20 at 1.1629 and SMA200 at 1.1637 while anchored above the SMA50 at 1.1529. ECB holds at 2.5%. Cross-asset dynamics show US Treasury yields bear-steepening with the 2s10s curve at +51.4bp and 10Y yields up to 4.944%, strengthening dollar rate insulation against surging oil costs. CFTC data reflects EUR leveraged funds net short -52,784 contracts (31st percentile, z=-0.39σ), indicating neutral institutional positioning. Options 25-delta risk reversals sit flat at -0.06 with modest IV of 5.0% over HV30 of 4.0% (VRP +1.0%), signaling lack of directional options participation as US rate dominance limits upside follow-through. Trade bias: Bearish EUR/USD; US yield-curve steepening and carry deficit cap upward progress. Catalyst: ECB President Lagarde speech at 08:00 UTC today. Risk: Spot prints a daily close above the SMA200 at 1.1637, dismantling the yield-driven ceiling.
